posts.title: Adjacent works and existing structure stability: temporary conditions still decide the outcome
posts.excerpt: Homes remain evacuated in Charlton after a partial frontage collapse near a regeneration site; the cause is under investigation. CROSS and HSE material keep showing the same control points: temporary conditions, vibration, sequence changes and load paths through the existing structure must be designed, checked and held before work proceeds.
posts.linkedinReady:
Homes remain evacuated in Charlton after a partial frontage collapse near a regeneration site.

On Saturday 23 August the fascia of a wall fell from roof level on Woodland Terrace. About 20 households were affected. Residents report heavy vibration from nearby development works and had asked for work to be paused. The developer has stated that the cause has not been established and that it would be inappropriate to speculate while investigations continue. No injuries were reported.

That is exactly the right stance while the facts are gathered. What the wider public record already shows is that temporary conditions around existing structures are where many failures begin.

CROSS-UK Report 1539 (May 2026) recorded temporary propping for column replacement where the props themselves were adequate — but the existing RC beams and slab that formed the load path had not been checked and would have failed in bending and shear. CROSS-UK Report 1479 (January 2026) showed a contractor sequence change on a bridge deck that introduced lateral-torsional buckling under wet concrete at over 200 % utilisation without temporary restraints. CROSS-UK Report 1486 (November 2025) described partial collapse during underpinning after intermediate floors and walls had been removed, destabilising the building before temporary works were in place.

HSE’s June 2026 Paxton House prosecution remains a clear UK reminder: temporary platforms collecting debris, no design, no calculated safe load, inspection not by a competent Temporary Works Coordinator.

For contractors and TWCs the practical message is unchanged:
• Adjacent excavation, piling, demolition or heavy plant near existing buildings belongs on the Temporary Works Register.
• Design briefs must capture vibration limits, monitoring, sequence and the capacity of the existing structure that will carry temporary loads.
• Sequence changes are design changes — they require review before work continues.
• Hold points (permit-to-load, competent inspection) close before load, debris or people are applied.

Educational only — not for construction; subject to the project temporary works procedure.

https://www.temporaryworksconsulting.com/news.html

#TemporaryWorks #BS5975 #CROSS #HSE #StructuralStability #ConstructionSafety #TWC

body.h: What is publicly reported from Charlton
body.p: On the evening of Saturday 23 August 2026 the frontage of two houses on Woodland Terrace, Charlton, partially collapsed. London Fire Brigade reported that the fascia of a wall fell from roof level. About 20 households were affected; seven were placed in temporary accommodation. Residents remain unable to return pending structural surveys. One resident stated that he had raised concerns about heavy vibration from nearby development works on the Woolwich Estates regeneration project and had requested that work be paused. The developer, Lovell, has said the cause of the collapse has not been established and that it would be inappropriate to speculate while investigations continue. Greenwich Council is working to understand the circumstances. No injuries were reported.

body.h: What CROSS and HSE already show about temporary conditions and existing structures
body.p: Published CROSS and HSE material continues to highlight the same control gaps. CROSS-UK Report 1539 (14 May 2026) concerned temporary works to allow removal of a defective reinforced concrete column. The proposed props were capable of taking the required forces, but no evidence was found that the prop designer had checked the existing RC beams and slab that formed the load path; those elements would have failed in bending and shear under the applied loads. CROSS-UK Report 1479 (13 January 2026) recorded a contractor change to the construction sequence on an approximately 20 m span filler-beam bridge deck: beams were to be lifted individually rather than in connected pairs, introducing a significant temporary lateral-torsional buckling risk under wet concrete. Without temporary restraints the utilisation exceeded 200 %. CROSS-UK Report 1486 (20 November 2025) described a partial collapse overnight during underpinning after the principal contractor had removed portions of intermediate internal floors and walls, destabilising the building. The Paxton House prosecution published by HSE on 15 June 2026 concerned temporary timber platforms under floor openings that collapsed under concrete debris; there was no design, no calculated safe load, and the inspection was not completed by a competent Temporary Works Coordinator.

body.h: Why temporary conditions decide the outcome
body.p: Existing structures carry temporary loads, vibration and sequence effects that are not present in the permanent design case. Adjacent piling, excavation, demolition, heavy plant movement or debris platforms alter those conditions. BS 5975-1:2024 management procedures place the Temporary Works Coordinator at the centre of identifying these items, issuing a design brief that captures sequence and existing structure, ensuring an appropriate design and check, and holding permit-to-load and competent inspection before the critical load state is reached. A verbal assurance or an inspection form completed by someone who is not competent for the item does not close the control.

body.h: What a competent contractor and TWC should check this week
ul: Identify every live interface with existing occupied or adjacent structures (excavation, piling, demolition, heavy plant, vibration-producing operations) and confirm it is on the Temporary Works Register.
Ensure design briefs for propping, platforms, shoring or sequence-critical works explicitly require assessment of the existing structure that will carry temporary loads or be affected by vibration.
Treat any proposed change to construction sequence as a temporary works design change requiring review before work proceeds.
Confirm that crash decks, debris platforms and working platforms have a design or justified standard solution, a posted safe load and inspection by a person competent for that item.
Where vibration or ground movement is foreseeable, agree monitoring and trigger levels with the temporary works designer and act on them.
